# Reference Selection

## Purpose

Decide, per page, the smallest set of approved images that holds the style,
the identities, the wardrobe, the space, and the props in place, and say what
each image is there to do. Every attached image has exactly one role. An image
model treats an unlabelled reference as a suggestion about everything at once,
which is how a style sample ends up donating its face to a character.

## Use When

- A page is scripted, its ledger is clean, and prompts are about to be
  compiled.
- `/reference-plan`, `/smart-page`, or `/generate-pages` finds a page without
  a plan.
- The provider changes and its reference limit is different.
- A review traced an identity or style failure to a missing or misused
  reference.

## Inputs

- `production/issues/<ISS_ID>/pages/<PG_ID>/page.yaml`: the drawn cast of
  every panel, `location`, held and visible props, the `references` block
  (`required`, `optional`), and `continuity.attach_previous_render`.
- `production/references/manifest.yaml`: asset `status`, `entity`, `kind`,
  `path`, and `default_role`.
- `production/project.yaml`: `style.look_refs` and
  `default_providers.image`.
- `character.yaml` (`references`, `visually_adjacent_to`) and `wardrobe.yaml`
  (`references` per outfit).
- The provider's `capabilities.referenceImages` in
  `manifests/image-providers.json`.
- The review file of the previous page's current render.

## Process

1. Read the page. List every character drawn in any panel (rows without
   `off_panel: true`), the location, each prop that is held or `visible`,
   and the wardrobe ID on each row.
2. Resolve each entity to assets in the manifest and keep only those with
   `status: approved`. Take the highest approved version. A draft or
   superseded asset in a plan is a defect.
3. Add the look master first: the asset in `style.look_refs`, role `style`,
   priority `critical`. It goes on every request, with no exceptions for
   pages that "obviously" match. The frozen style block repeats the words.
   Only the image holds the line.
4. Add one identity reference per drawn character: the approved turnaround
   or sheet, role `identity`, priority `critical`. When two characters on
   the page list each other in `visually_adjacent_to`, both references stay,
   whatever else has to go.
5. Add a wardrobe reference (role `wardrobe`) from the outfit's `references`.
   It is required when the outfit worn on this page is not the character's
   `default_wardrobe`. For the default outfit it is optional, because the
   identity sheet already shows it.
6. Add spatial references with role `spatial_continuity`, as optional
   entries: the previous page's current render when `attach_previous_render`
   is true, and the location plate when the page has a view wide enough to
   show the place. Rank the previous page above the plate.
7. Attach a previous page only after its review. Open its review file and
   confirm the verdict is `pass` or `fixed`. A page that has not been
   reviewed, or that is flagged, passes its defects on to every page
   conditioned on it. The first page of an issue has no previous render.
8. Add prop references (role `prop_consistency`) for plot-relevant props
   drawn on the page that have a registered image. Skip incidental dressing.
9. Use role `composition` only for a registered layout reference the page
   must follow. Role `edit_target` belongs to repairs: `page-repair` names
   the flagged render as the image being edited, and a first-generation plan
   never contains one.
10. Give every entry one role and list every asset once. If one image seems
    to serve two purposes, pick the purpose it is approved for and find or
    make another image for the other.
11. Fit the budget. `budget` is the provider's reference limit. Rank entries
    `critical`, `high`, `medium`, `low`. Optional entries that do not fit
    are dropped from the lowest priority up and listed in `exclude`, with
    the reason in `notes`. If the required entries alone exceed the budget,
    stop. Choose a provider with a higher limit, generate per panel
    (`generation.mode: per_panel`), or split the page, and bring the choice
    to the user. Moving a character off panel to save an image changes the
    staging: propose it with the reason, never make it silently.
    `check-continuity.js` already warns about this at plan time
    (`REFERENCE_BUDGET`), per page and per panel.
12. Exclude anything that contradicts the page: an outfit from another
    scene, a plate of the location at another time of day, a superseded
    sheet.
13. Write the page's `references.required` and `references.optional`, then
    run `node scripts/build-reference-plan.js --page <page.yaml>`, adding
    `--provider <id>` to plan for a provider other than the default. Read
    the file it writes against steps 3 to 12. When the selection is wrong,
    correct the inputs and run it again. Sharpen `reason` and
    `omission_risk` by hand last. The plan records the `generation.mode`,
    provider and budget it was built for; `compile-prompts.js` rebuilds it
    when one of them changes, which replaces hand edits, so put lasting
    choices in `references.required` and `references.optional` instead.

## Outputs

`production/issues/<ISS_ID>/pages/<PG_ID>/reference-plan.yaml`
(`reference-plan.schema.json`). Example for the second page of the sample
story:

```yaml
page: PG_001_002
provider: harness-native
budget: 4
mode: full_page
required:
  - asset_id: LOOK_NOIR_INK_MASTER_V01
    entity: LOOK_NOIR_INK
    role: style
    priority: critical
    reason: Fixed drawing style for every request.
    omission_risk: Style drifts toward the model's default.
  - asset_id: CHAR_MARA_TURN_MASTER_V01
    entity: CHAR_MARA
    role: identity
    priority: critical
    reason: Mara is drawn in all four panels.
    omission_risk: Her broken nose and cropped hair get reinvented.
  - asset_id: CHAR_OSKAR_TURN_MASTER_V01
    entity: CHAR_OSKAR
    role: identity
    priority: critical
    reason: Oskar is revealed here and is listed as visually adjacent to Mara.
    omission_risk: The boy inherits Mara's face.
optional:
  - asset_id: PG_001_001_V01
    entity: null
    role: spatial_continuity
    priority: high
    reason: Reviewed previous page; holds the deck, the crates, and the bow on screen left.
    omission_risk: The ladder and crates change sides.
exclude: [LOC_FERRY_DECK_PLATE_MASTER_V01]
created_at: "2026-11-26"
notes: "LOC_FERRY_DECK_PLATE_MASTER_V01 left out: budget of 4 reached, and the previous page already carries the space."
```

Three required images and one optional fill the budget of four. The plate
was the lowest-priority optional entry, so it moved to `exclude`.

## Quality Bar

- The look master is in `required` with role `style` on every page.
- Every drawn character has exactly one `identity` entry.
- Every entry has one role, a reason, and a priority, and no asset appears
  twice.
- Every asset cited is `approved` in the manifest at the version cited.
- A previous-page render appears only when its review verdict is `pass` or
  `fixed`.
- The `required` entries fit inside `budget`, and every excluded asset has
  its reason in `notes`.
- Every drawn entity is referenced, or its absence is recorded with the risk.

## Common Failure Modes

- The style image left off because the prompt "already says noir ink".
  Repeating a style word is not a substitute for the look master.
- One image used as both style and identity, and the character takes on the
  face in the style sample.
- Every slot filled to be safe, so the identity references compete with
  noise.
- The previous page attached before anyone opened it, carrying a wrong face
  into the next three pages.
- A secondary character with no reference at all, who then borrows the
  nearest face.
- A required reference dropped silently when the budget ran out.
- A wardrobe reference from a different outfit state than the one on the
  page.

## Notes

The plan is the bridge between the bibles and the prompt. `prompt-compilation`
attaches only the images this plan lists, in this order of priority, and
states in words what any omitted reference would have shown.

Names do not prevent identity substitution. When two characters could blend,
the plan supplies both sheets and the prompt states the visible difference
between them.
